author: sprine
body: This pull request includes significant changes to the project, primarily focused on improving the representation of sketches and their metadata, and automating the process of analyzing sketches and generating metadata using an AI model. The most important changes are: 1. Adding a new JSON file `all_sketches.json` that contains metadata for multiple sketches, including stylistic words, title, file name, description, differences between the sketch and today's reality, insights, keywords, and file details. 2. Adding a new Python script `cli.py` that automates the process of analyzing sketches and generating metadata using an AI model. The script includes functions for preparing images for the AI model, sending images to the AI model and receiving responses, encoding images to base64, converting SVG images to PNG, and processing SVG files. 3. Updating `index.html` to dynamically render sketches and their metadata from `all_sketches.json`. The updated file includes new styles and scripts for fetching the JSON file, creating a container for each sketch, adding an SVG or PNG image for the sketch, adding a title block with the sketch's title and a close button, and adding details including the description, keywords, insights, and differences. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051L4-L13) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051L31-R30) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051R47-R159) ### cli usage ``` python cli.py sketches/IMG_2661.JPG ``` ### run server; load all files ``` (base) ➜ sketches git:(proto1-multiple-on-one-page) ✗ python -m http.server Serving HTTP on :: port 8000 (http://[::]:8000/) ... ::1 - - [03/Jul/2024 18:30:20] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 - ::1 - - [03/Jul/2024 18:30:20] "GET /js/svg-pan-zoom.min.js HTTP/1.1" 200 - ::1 - - [03/Jul/2024 18:30:20] "GET /js/d3.v7.min.js HTTP/1.1" 200 - ::1 - - [03/Jul/2024 18:30:21] "GET /js/sketchviz.js HTTP/1.1" 200 - ::1 - - [03/Jul/2024 18:30:21] "GET /all_sketches.json HTTP/1.1" 200 - ::1 - - [03/Jul/2024 18:30:21] "GET /static/IMG_2657.jpeg HTTP/1.1" 200 - ::1 - - [03/Jul/2024 18:30:21] "GET /static/IMG_2661.JPG HTTP/1.1" 200 - ::1 - - [03/Jul/2024 18:30:21] "GET /static/IMG_2660.JPG HTTP/1.1" 200 - ::1 - - [03/Jul/2024 18:30:21] "GET /static/gamify.excalidraw.svg HTTP/1.1" 200 - ::1 - - [03/Jul/2024 18:30:21] "GET /static/IMG_2662.JPG HTTP/1.1" 200 - ::1 - - [03/Jul/2024 18:30:21] "GET /static/IMG_2663.JPG HTTP/1.1" 200 - ::1 - - [03/Jul/2024 18:30:21] "GET /static/learning.svg HTTP/1.1" 200 - ::1 - - [03/Jul/2024 18:30:21] "GET /static/mental%20health%20explorer.jpg HTTP/1.1" 200 - ``` ### What's worked well? The summaries are absolutely incredible, given just a simple prompt and zero additional context. This technology feels like my closest encounter to a black magic function yet. I like the title block quite a lot. I learned the word "title block" from architecture drawings. It meshes well with sketching. ![image](https://github.com/sprine/sketches/assets/818810/67b23bf4-84ea-492c-8817-41e3b5899822) I also like the section collapse and the opacity change when collapsing. - The continuous page scroll isn't bad. - _Tags_ are delightful and themes are already starting to emerge. - _Insights_ are excellent too. They're not really insights though -- they're more like "logical conclusions" or "patterns" -- is that what "insights" are? ### What's not working? - the page size is very large because images are not compressed or scaled. It could easily be brought down. - the svg zoom feature takes over the mouse when scrolled over. Have to move over the title block or screen edges to recover control. I don't think svg viewer + continuous image scroll work well together. - the continuous page scroll isn't good because there is no indication of much there is to scroll. Even the simplest of indicators would help. - _Reality check_ isn't as useful as I'd originally hoped. The original idea was that it could help explain gaps between a fleshed out conceptual model vs the real world. However, the sketches are expected to be rough, and the reality check isn't necessarily detailed enough. ### What else have I learned in the experiment? `gpt-4o` baffles me. The fact that it could explain the "Mental map of Learning" sketch was a turning point. It's made me realize that this ability by `gpt-4o` applied to sketches fits in an unique space: Sketches seem to provide an exceptional way to describe the context. This is obviously not new: > "A picture is worth a thousand words" is an adage in multiple languages meaning that complex and sometimes multiple ideas[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_picture_is_worth_a_thousand_words#cite_note-1) can be conveyed by a single still image, which conveys its meaning or essence more effectively than a mere verbal description. Very cool to see it actually apply in this case.

author: mxyng
body:
current envconfig is configured on import by `init()`. this is problematic and error prone in tests which sometimes override configurations. which means the test must call `envconfig.LoadConfig()` otherwise it'll have side effects

e.g.
```go
func TestRemoveModels(t *testing.T) {
    t.Setenv("OLLAMA_MODELS", t.TempDir())
    // envconfig.LoadConfig()

    RemoveModels()
}
```

this pattern is repeated in many tests but anyone writing a new test can easily miss it

this change proposes a new envconfig where configurations are functions rather than variables. this allows dynamic lookup of configurations while keeping the same-ish interface

Related to Automattic/i18n-issues#835


## Why are these changes being made?
<!--
It's easy to see what a PR does but much harder to find out why it was made,
particularly when researching old changes in history. Record an explanation of
the motivation behind this change and how it will help.
-->

In this PR, I've added the capability for translators to localize date formats.

Previously, I explored browser-based solutions such as [Intl.DateTimeFormat](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl/DateTimeFormat/DateTimeFormat) and [Date.toLocaleDateString](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Date/toLocaleDateString).

However, these methods proved inadequate for our needs because their dateStyle options do not support the `MMMM YYYY` format. Both dateStyle: 'medium' and dateStyle: 'long' include the day in the format (e.g., July **3**, 2024), which is not desirable for our use case.

More info in [Memoizing with create-selector](https://github.com/Automattic/wp-calypso/blob/trunk/packages/state-utils/src/create-selector/README.md) and [Using memoizing selectors](https://react-redux.js.org/api/hooks#using-memoizing-selectors) and [Our Approach to Data](https://github.com/Automattic/wp-calypso/blob/trunk/docs/our-approach-to-data.md)
- [x] Have we added the "[Status] String Freeze" label as soon as any new strings were ready for translation (p4TIVU-5Jq-p2)?
